rationale: Burst supply line to the policyholder's own bathroom is a plumbing failure within the insured premises that caused damage to the basement structure (hardwood floor, drywall) and contents (boxes), clearly fitting property_damage coverage.
claim_summary: Sam Patel (POL-1004) has basement flooding damage caused by a burst supply line under the bathroom sink that ran for approximately two days. Damage includes two inches of standing water, buckled hardwood floors, soaked drywall (up to one foot), and ruined stored boxes. This is a high-severity claim (estimated damage likely exceeds $25,000) requiring immediate adjuster dispatch for mitigation and detailed assessment.

case_facts.incident_date: While policyholder was away on work trip; burst pipe ran for approximately two days
case_facts.description: Supply line under upstairs bathroom sink burst; water flowed into basement for two days before discovery
case_facts.damage_details: Two inches of water across entire basement; hardwood floor buckled; drywall soaked up to one foot; multiple stored boxes ruined
case_facts.cause: Burst supply line under bathroom sink (policyholder's plumbing)

rationale: Wind-driven damage to the policyholder's own roof structure is straightforward property damage covered under a homeowners policy.
claim_summary: Wind damage claim from Jordan Lee (POL-1006): approximately four shingles blown off back porch overhang last weekend. Estimated repair cost $400 with no interior water damage. Deductible $2,500 applies.

case_facts.description: four shingles blown off by wind, no interior water damage
